description:
PF12 - app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:123-125, the UNCONDITIONAL exit to the admin menu, and the one case that keeps DFHPF12 from silently collapsing into WHEN OTHER. EIBCALEN is 194 so :94 copies the area in, CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT is 1 so :95 sends the flow down the re-entry branch, :107 performs RECEIVE-USRDEL-SCREEN, and the ordered EVALUATE EIBAID at :108-130 matches its FIFTH arm - DFHENTER at :109, then DFHPF3 at :111, DFHPF4 at :119, DFHPF5 at :121, DFHPF12 at :123, and WHEN OTHER last at :126, first match winning. That the DFHPF12 arm sits AFTER DFHPF5 is part of the ordered-arm contract, so what is asserted here is that PF12 is matched by its OWN arm and not by WHEN OTHER: falling through would move CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY into WS-MESSAGE and paint a screen instead of navigating, and that is a realistic failure mode precisely because DFHAID is IBM-supplied and ABSENT from this repository, so DFHPF12 is reproduced in common/CicsAid as 0x7C from IBM CICS documentation rather than read from a copybook. THE DIVERGENCE THIS CASE EXISTS TO PIN: :124 moves 'COADM01C' into CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM with NO test of CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, where the DFHPF3 arm at :112 does test it. CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is therefore supplied POPULATED here, as 'COUSR00C', and must be IGNORED: nextProgram is 'COADM01C' and not 'COUSR00C'. A nextProgram of 'COUSR00C' would mean the PF3 sub-condition had been wrongly applied to PF12, and with a blank predecessor the two arms would produce identical output and a translation that conflated them would pass - which is why case16 pins PF3 with a blank predecessor, case17 pins PF3 with this same populated one, and this case changes exactly ONE input byte against case17, the AID, so that the difference is observable. CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM is additionally supplied BLANK on input, which arms the :199-201 default and separates a third failure mode: a nextProgram of 'COSGN00C' would mean :124 never ran at all. Supplying it blank also keeps the case honest, because the expected target is then nowhere among the inputs and nothing here can pass by asserting a value it was handed. RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN at :197-208 then runs in source order: the :199-201 guard is FALSE because :124 has just set CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM, so the 'COSGN00C' default is BYPASSED; :202 writes CDEMO-FROM-TRANID from WS-TRANID as 'CU03'; :203 writes CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM from WS-PGMNAME as 'COUSR03C', OVERWRITING the 'COUSR00C' that arrived, so that one field's input and output values differ and both are pinned; :204 writes CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT from MOVE ZEROS as 0, handing the next program a fresh ENTER context; and :205-208 XCTLs. The XCTL is projected as a nextProgram response field, statelessly - no server-side forward, no redirect chain, no session affinity and no server-side session state of any kind: the commarea, the AID and the screen values all travel in the payload and the client issues the follow-up call - and every other carried item passes through untouched, which is why all 22 are pinned item by item rather than left implicit. SEND-USRDEL-SCREEN is never performed, so sends is empty and no map is painted, no cursor is requested, and nextMapset and nextMap are reported ABSENT rather than blank because :205-208 names a program and leaves the map and mapset untouched; the EXEC CICS RETURN at :134 is never reached because the XCTL transfers control. No error arises, so there is no message text and no DFHRED-plus-'*' highlight: COUSR03C copies neither CSSETATY nor CSSTRPFY, sets its attributes inline, and moves exactly one attribute item, ERRMSGC, at :285 and :317, neither of which is on this path. The two BLANK lines in expectedMessages assert precisely that absence of text, and they are neither an omission nor an invention: :87-88 move SPACES to WS-MESSAGE and to ERRMSGO OF COUSR3AO UNCONDITIONALLY and BEFORE the :90 EIBCALEN test, so an 80-character and a 78-character blank line are genuinely observable on this path, and each is pinned on its own channel at its own declared width so that the 80-to-78 truncation of MOVE WS-MESSAGE TO ERRMSGO cannot hide. case01, case16 and case17 pin them identically. USRSEC is seeded although this path never touches it, so that 'nothing was written' is a POSITIVE assertion rather than an absence of interest: expectedWrites is empty and all ten rows are pinned UNCHANGED at zero-based indices 0-9, each as its six CSUSR01Y fields and as its full 80-byte image, which is what proves a navigation path performs no I/O. NO repository interaction is declared because none happens - there is NO call site on this path for a FILE STATUS or RESP outcome to be forced at - and none is fabricated for a call that never occurs. The RECEIVE at :232-238 does capture RESP and RESP2 into WS-RESP-CD and WS-REAS-CD, and the program never evaluates them; that is preserved exactly as written and no receive-failure branch is invented. A second preserved divergence is worth recording rather than repairing: the BMS key legend at app/bms/COUSR03.bms:148 reads 'ENTER=Fetch  F3=Back  F4=Clear  F5=Delete' and OMITS F12 entirely, yet the program handles DFHPF12 at :123-125. The legend is not corrected, and PF12 is not treated as unreachable, because this case drives that code path. The payload contract is the eleven xxxI items of app/cpy-bms/COUSR03.CPY and nothing else - TRNNAMEI X(4), TITLE01I X(40), CURDATEI X(8), PGMNAMEI X(8), TITLE02I X(40), CURTIMEI X(8), USRIDINI X(8), FNAMEI X(20), LNAMEI X(20), USRTYPEI X(1), ERRMSGI X(78) - eleven exactly, with NO password item anywhere in the mapset, and with the xxxL, xxxF and xxxA items remaining length, flag and attribute METADATA rather than payload members. The one map field declared is USRIDINI, spelt USRIDIN and not USERID, carrying what the operator had typed before pressing the exit key; the clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:35 exactly as case01 pins it, so nothing non-deterministic enters the fixture. Four gates do not apply here: this program has no backward loop-forming GO TO, no CALL 'CEE3ABD' and therefore RETURN-CODE 0, no pagination arithmetic, and no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC optimistic-concurrency check. PROVENANCE: every value here is STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of the sources below and is NOT captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy COBOL - running it is empirically impossible in this environment, on eight independently verified blockers (no z/OS or CICS runtime; the available compiler reports its indexed-file handler disabled; PROCEDURE ... USING is rejected when an executable is requested; app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy carries literal TAB characters that break parsing; no Language Environment CEE* services exist; the 17 online programs are unrunnable at any level; the EBCDIC fixtures need binary handling the compiler is not configured for; and no alternative compiler is installable) - which is the documented deviation escalated for explicit user confirmation. It changes the PROVENANCE of the expected values and nothing else: 20 cases per program, field-for-field diffing, the diff-count-equals-zero gate per module and the branch-coverage bar are all preserved. Derived from app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:123-125 and :197-208, with :36-37 for WS-PGMNAME 'COUSR03C' and WS-TRANID 'CU03', :87-88 for the two blank lines, :108-130 for the arm order and :232-238 for the unevaluated RESP capture; cross-checked against app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:19-44 (4+8+4+8+8+1+1 = 34, plus 84 customer, 12 account, 16 card and 14 more-info = 160 bytes) plus app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:50-58 (the 34-byte CDEMO-CU03-INFO extension, carried in the DTO rather than folded into the shared 160-byte NavigationContext, 160 + 34 = 194 = EIBCALEN), app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 (SEC-USR-ID X(08) at 0, SEC-USR-FNAME X(20) at 8, SEC-USR-LNAME X(20) at 28, SEC-USR-PWD X(08) at 48, SEC-USR-TYPE X(01) at 56 - 8+20+20+8+1 = 57 - and SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) at 57, 57+23 = 80), app/cpy-bms/COUSR03.CPY and app/bms/COUSR03.bms:140-148, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD for TRANSACTION(CU03) PROGRAM(COUSR03C), and the ten in-stream rows of app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, whose 57-character width against the LRECL=80 RECFM=FB of :48 and the RECORDSIZE(80,80) KEYS(8,0) of :65-66 is exactly what the declared USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation supplies - the rows are held at their authored 57 characters and never pre-padded, and no tenth fixture file is introduced. SEC-USR-FILLER is asserted BY NAME as 23 spaces in all ten records, because a codec that dropped it would put every downstream offset and the total record width wrong. The literal PASSWORD in SEC-USR-PWD is legacy sample data carried byte for byte because the copybook places it inside the eighty bytes; plaintext credentials are an inherited property of the legacy design rather than a choice made here, this screen has no password field and never reads or paints the span, and no hashing, encoding or token is introduced. The dataset is addressed only by its USRSEC binding key and never by a literal dataset name. review_rules reports no user rules for this project, so no user rule governs this fixture; it is held instead to the enterprise practices B1-B12 of the plan.

THE OPERATION ORDER, DECLARED RATHER THAN INFERRED. expectedOperations names every USRSEC operation this case must issue, in order, and it is an assertion a byte fingerprint structurally cannot make: the EXEC CICS DELETE at app/cbl/COUSR03C.cbl:307-311 names no RIDFLD, so it removes the record the task is HOLDING and is only ever correct after the EXEC CICS READ ... UPDATE at :269-278 took that hold on the same record. An empty list is equally an assertion - it says this path never reached the file at all.
